formats.key: batchExecute((address to, uint256 value, bytes data)[] calls)
effects: Runs only by DELEGATECALL from the signer's Safe (line 50 reverts on a direct call), so every sub-call is made from the Safe's own account.
For each call i, sends calls[i].value of native currency from the Safe to calls[i].to.
For each call i, runs calls[i].data on calls[i].to with the Safe as msg.sender. That can move any of the Safe's tokens, set approvals, or change roles and settings, depending on the inner call.
Calls with empty data are allowed to any address, EOAs included (line 53). Those are plain native-currency transfers.
All-or-nothing: if any sub-call fails, the whole batch reverts with BatchExecutionFailed(i, errorData).
formats.shown: The intent 'Batch transactions', then one 'Transaction' calldata field per call. Each field is decoded with the inner descriptor for calls[].to, and calls[].value is passed in through amountPath. The target and value have no fields of their own.

findings.title: batchExecute: calls[].value (native currency leaving the Safe) is never its own field; empty-data transfers have no inner descriptor
findings.evidence: BatchExecutor.sol batchExecute: `calls[i].to.call{value: calls[i].value}(calls[i].data)`, and line 53 lets calls with `data.length == 0` go to any address. In the descriptor, the only field is `calls.[].data` with format calldata and params `amountPath: calls.[].value`. Under the spec, amountPath only passes the value to the inner descriptor, which 'MAY reference' @.value. For a plain native transfer (empty data) there is no selector and no inner descriptor, so no field shows the amount or the recipient.
findings.fix: Add per-call fields: `calls.[].to` labelled 'To' (addressName) and `calls.[].value` labelled 'Value' (format amount). Keep the calldata field.

findings.title: batchExecute: the intent 'Batch transactions' says nothing about the calls running as the Safe
findings.evidence: descriptor intent: "Batch transactions", with no interpolatedIntent. The code runs each call from the Safe through delegatecall (devdoc: 'It executes each call in the context of the calling Safe'). Each call can move Safe assets or change its settings, and the whole batch reverts if one call fails.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Execute batch of calls from this Safe', and add an interpolatedIntent if the runner supports counting calls.

findings.title: batchExecute: no spenderPath, so inner descriptors that read @.from cannot resolve the Safe as sender
findings.evidence: descriptor params hold only calleePath and amountPath. In the code, msg.sender of each sub-call is the Safe, because BatchExecutor runs by delegatecall. The spec says spenderPath supplies @.from to the embedded descriptor.
findings.fix: If the runner allows it, pass the account address (e.g. `spenderPath: @.from`) so inner descriptors see the Safe as sender.

findings.title: batchExecute: payable, but @.value has no field; under delegatecall from a Safe the top-level value is not what moves funds
findings.evidence: `function batchExecute(Call[] calldata calls) external payable`. Line 50 forces delegatecall, and a Safe delegatecall carries no value of its own. Native currency moves only through calls[i].value.
findings.fix: None needed beyond showing calls[].value per call.

findings.format: batchExecute((address to, uint256 value, bytes data)[] calls)
findings.title: batchExecute: calls[].value (native currency leaving the Safe) is never its own field; empty-data transfers have no inner descriptor
findings.reason: The contract runs in the Safe through delegatecall and sends `calls[i].value` of the Safe's native currency to `calls[i].to`. Nothing in the code limits that value. The descriptor has no field for `calls.[].value`. `amountPath` only passes the value to an inner descriptor, which under the spec 'MAY reference' `@.value`, and the spec's fallback when no inner descriptor matches shows only a calldata hash and the callee. A plain transfer with empty data has no selector, so no inner descriptor exists and nothing on screen shows the amount. This matches the guide's critical example of native currency leaving in an amount never shown, and the not-critical cases do not cover it: the amount is not shown anywhere else, and it is a fact, not a possibility.
findings.quote: BatchExecutor.sol batchExecute: `(bool success, bytes memory errorData) = calls[i].to.call{value: calls[i].value}(calls[i].data);` and line 53 `if (calls[i].to.code.length == 0 && calls[i].data.length > 0) revert` (this only blocks data sent to EOAs, so a call with empty data to any address goes through). descriptor.json batchExecute: the only field is `{"path": "calls.[].data", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "calls.[].to", "amountPath": "calls.[].value"}}`

findings.format: batchExecute((address to, uint256 value, bytes data)[] calls)
findings.title: batchExecute: calls[].value (native currency leaving the Safe) is never its own field; empty-data transfers have no inner descriptor
findings.reason: An empty-data call with nonzero value transfers the Safe’s native currency without displaying its amount. The fallback can show the recipient, so the recipient-omission claim is overstated, but the hidden amount confirms the critical finding.
findings.quote: contracts/1-0x2cc8475177918e8c4d840150b68815a4b6f0f5f3/src/BatchExecutor.sol, batchExecute: `if (calls[i].to.code.length == 0 && calls[i].data.length > 0)` rejects only nonempty data to non-contracts; `(bool success, bytes memory errorData) = calls[i].to.call{value: calls[i].value}(calls[i].data);` sends the value. descriptor.json, batchExecute: `"intent": "Batch transactions"`; the sole field is `"path": "calls.[].data", "label": "Transaction", "format": "calldata", "params": {"calleePath": "calls.[].to", "amountPath": "calls.[].value"}`. Registry specs/erc-7730.md, calldata format: the embedded descriptor `MAY reference this value using the @.value container path`; unresolved calldata `MAY display a hash ... with target calleePath resolved to a trusted name if possible`.
